text.deployment: The standard Hetzer is found throughout the Inner Sphere, concentrated most heavily in militia and planetary defense roles. Its low cost and simple maintenance requirements make it accessible to governments that cannot afford professional combined-arms formations. It is most commonly deployed in pairs or larger groups to compensate for the lack of a turret and limited armor, relying on massed firepower to achieve results that no single vehicle could accomplish alone.

The AC/10 variant arose as supply chains for the heavy Crusher cannon became unreliable during the Succession Wars. Commanders accepted reduced hitting power in exchange for improved sustainability, as AC/10 rounds were more widely available than AC/20 ammunition. It served primarily in the same militia and garrison roles as the standard model, offering a cheaper logistical footprint at the cost of significant firepower reduction.

The most significant redesign in the Hetzer's history, the Cell variant replaces the ICE powerplant with a fuel cell and adopts dual-autocannon armament, distributing firepower across two systems and improving reliability. Produced at Broken Wheel, Indicass, and Layover under the Federated Vilalobos Corporation network, the variant is available to both FVC-affiliated forces and Capellan customers. It retains the Hetzer's low cost and simple maintenance profile while meaningfully improving performance.

Introduced almost simultaneously with the base model, the laser variant substitutes medium lasers for the Crusher cannon. Local commands producing this configuration typically lacked ammunition supply chains but had access to power generation infrastructure. Found throughout the Inner Sphere wherever heat management is acceptable and autocannon rounds are unavailable, it trades the Hetzer's one-shot punch for sustainable energy fire.

Produced exclusively at the Ceres Metals Industries facility on Indicass, the LB-X variant equipped the Capellan Confederation with a version capable of engaging BattleMechs and battle armor at close ranges with cluster munitions. The weapon improved the Hetzer's effectiveness in anti-personnel and light-armor roles. The variant was phased out following the arrival of the Predator Tank Destroyer, which performed the same function more effectively on an improved platform.

A less common field modification, the LRM variant allows the Hetzer to engage at longer ranges, partially compensating for the chassis's inability to rotate its weapon. The vehicle's thin armor still demands concealment or defilade, but the extended engagement range provides more tactical flexibility in placement. Found occasionally across the Inner Sphere wherever long-range missile ammunition supply is reliable.

A Word of Blake Protectorate refit, the Sealed variant adds a C3i computer network and replaces the primary weapon with a Rotary Autocannon inside an NBC-sealed hull, allowing operations in chemically or biologically contaminated environments. The C3i system links the RAC to supporting units, substantially increasing coordinated accuracy. After the Jihad, the design spread through salvage and knowledge transfer, entering small-scale Universal production through the Dark Age.

The SRM variant replaces the primary cannon with short-range missiles, giving the Hetzer a more flexible if shorter-ranged weapons package. Short-range missile ammunition is widely available throughout the Inner Sphere, making this variant viable in supply-constrained environments. It is most commonly found in Capellan Confederation and associated militia forces, where the modification is performed at the unit level.

Developed by Clan Wolf after acquiring the Kalidasa production line, the C variant mounts a Hyper-Assault Gauss rifle in place of the autocannon, extending the basic Hetzer chassis into Clan-technology performance tiers. It provides Clan Wolf warriors an inexpensive long-range fire platform suited to garrison and support roles. The Rasalhague Dominion independently refitted Hetzers on Alshain through Joint Equipment Systems, producing the same Clan-armed configuration for Dominion toumans.

text.overview: The Hi-Scout Drone Carrier is a sixty-ton tracked reconnaissance vehicle produced by ScolTek Associates on Inarcs for the Lyran Commonwealth beginning in 3000. Designed as a mobile command hub for a network of unmanned sensor drones, the Hi-Scout offered planetary garrison forces a cost-effective alternative to committing BattleMechs or manned scout vehicles to forward reconnaissance. The vehicle serves as both the control platform and transport for its complement of six drones, coordinating their movements and processing their sensor data into actionable intelligence for field commanders. Produced initially for the LCAF, the Hi-Scout earned a reputation as one of the most capable dedicated reconnaissance systems of the late Succession Wars era, filling a niche that few other designs attempted to address. ScolTek's facility on Inarcs has maintained continuous production for over eight decades, making the Hi-Scout one of the longest-running vehicle programs in Lyran service.
text.capabilities:
The Hi-Scout's primary strength lies in its StealthMat-Q communications system with MultiTrack coordination, capable of transmitting and monitoring over five hundred channels simultaneously. This allows the vehicle's crew to control six drones, three NapFind hover types and three PathTrak tracked types, carried in a fifteen-ton internal drone hangar. The drones create an overlapping sensor chain that more than doubles the carrier's effective detection range. The vehicle's own sensor suite includes infrared, seismic, audio, motion, radio (including hyperpulse signals), and radar, providing comprehensive coverage within sixty kilometers even without drone support.

Defensively, the Hi-Scout carries only a single SureShot II SRM-2 launcher with one ton of ammunition, reflecting its role as a rear-echelon asset rather than a frontline combatant. Five and a half tons of ArcShield V armor offer limited protection, sufficient to survive encounters with light hovercraft but inadequate against anything heavier. The Vlar 240 internal combustion engine provides a top speed of 64 kilometers per hour, adequate for keeping pace with infantry formations but leaving the vehicle vulnerable if forced to withdraw under fire. The designers clearly prioritized sensor capability and drone coordination over survivability, accepting that the vehicle must rely on friendly forces for protection.
text.deployment: The standard Hi-Scout Drone Carrier serves as the foundation of ScolTek's reconnaissance system. Deployed primarily with LCAF garrison forces and planetary militia commands, the vehicle operates from the rear echelon of defensive positions, directing its drone network to establish sensor coverage across threatened approach corridors. The Hi-Scout's effectiveness depends heavily on terrain and electromagnetic conditions, performing best in open environments with low background radiation where the MultiTrack coordination system can maintain reliable contact with all six drones simultaneously. Garrison commanders typically deploy Hi-Scouts in pairs to provide overlapping coverage and redundancy, with each vehicle responsible for a separate sector of the defensive perimeter.
text.battleHistory:
ScolTek Associates introduced the Hi-Scout Drone Carrier to fill a specific gap in LCAF reconnaissance doctrine. During the late Third Succession War, the technological decline that characterized the era had left most planetary garrisons without reliable surveillance capabilities. Satellite networks were degraded or absent on many worlds, and committing BattleMechs to scouting roles was increasingly untenable given their growing scarcity. The Hi-Scout offered a middle path, deploying expendable drones to gather intelligence while keeping the carrier vehicle and its trained crew safely behind friendly lines.

The system proved its value quickly after entering service, and ScolTek soon found that demand outstripped their production capacity. A broad range of copycat vehicles emerged after the first LCAF Hi-Scouts were captured in a Kurita raid, and scores of ScolTek-produced units were smuggled to other Successor States through various intermediaries posing as mercenary buyers. Within less than twenty years, nearly all five Great Houses possessed Hi-Scout drone networks or effective knock-offs using similar designs. Though the Lyran Intelligence Corps eventually plugged the security breaches that had made this proliferation possible, by 3025 the strategic advantage ScolTek's innovation had originally provided to House Steiner had largely evaporated.

ScolTek maintained steady production on Inarcs throughout the Clan Invasion and Civil War periods. The company's fortunes survived the Jihad intact, suffering no damage from the Word of Blake or other hostile forces, and the factory was operating at full capacity by the end of 3079. The recovery of Star League technology and the development of C3 networking placed the original Hi-Scout design on the table for significant upgrades. ScolTek's engineering staff eventually pursued an ambitious modernization program, producing experimental prototypes that incorporated XL engine technology, enhanced ECM systems, and C3 integration to bring the platform into the modern era.

text.overview:
The Hipparch Cavalry Tank was commissioned in 2562 on the direct orders of First Consul Gregory Amaris of the Rim Worlds Republic, conceived as a fast, aggressive platform to project Republican military power. Designed and built by Diplass Technologies on Apollo, the vehicle was intended to provide the Rim Worlds Army with a capable cavalry asset competitive with Inner Sphere and Star League designs of its day.

Amaris personally championed the program and ordered thousands produced, though critics within the military argued that political considerations rather than battlefield requirements drove the design. The Hipparch's impressive top speed gave Republic cavalry formations genuine offensive potential, but the design's numerous compromises ultimately defined its legacy as much as its battlefield performance.
text.capabilities:
The Hipparch's defining characteristic is its exceptional speed, reaching 151 kph on the hover skirt using the Mercury 140 power plant. This velocity made the vehicle one of the fastest combat platforms of its era, allowing Republican cavalry to conduct high-speed raids, screening operations, and pursuit missions that most opponents could not match.

Armament consists of a pair of Diplass Optimax lasers, one medium and one small, paired with a Harvester SRM 2 missile rack carrying a single ton of reloads. The mix offers reasonable versatility for scout and harassment work, though the payload is modest for a vehicle of its size. Mounting energy weapons on an ICE-powered hull required additional power conversion and heat dissipation equipment, consuming mass that critics argued would have been better spent on armor or firepower.

The resulting protection is thin, only four tons of Forge 9 Flexweave armor distributed with a slight bias toward the front and sides. This proved inadequate against sustained fire from most opponents. Combined with quality control deficiencies from rushed production, the Hipparch's survivability in a stand-up engagement was genuinely poor, requiring crews to rely on speed and maneuver rather than durability.
text.deployment:
The base-model Hipparch served the Rim Worlds Army primarily as a cavalry and scout vehicle during the Reunification War. Its operational profile centered on high-speed reconnaissance, flank screening, and pursuit missions where its velocity offered a decisive advantage. The vehicle's light armament was suited to harassment and anti-infantry duty, though crews frequently improvised field modifications, mounting machine guns for anti-infantry work or trading energy weapons for a larger missile payload.

The most extreme field modification, nicknamed the "Hellhorse" by troops, replaced the entire weapon payload and turret assembly with explosives, converting the vehicle into a crude kamikaze weapon driven into enemy formations or encampments. No factory-built variants were ever produced. With the production line destroyed in 2599, surviving Hipparchs soldiered on until attrition claimed the last of them.
text.battleHistory:
The Hipparch entered service in 2562 as part of First Consul Gregory Amaris's broader effort to modernize the Rim Worlds Army ahead of the Republic's involvement in the Reunification War. Diplass Technologies delivered thousands of vehicles in rapid succession, with production timelines prioritized over quality assurance. Manufacturing defects and field breakdowns accumulated before the design ever reached combat, setting the stage for the problems that would follow.

When Reunification War operations began in 2577, the Hipparch served as the Republic's primary cavalry asset. In reconnaissance and screening roles the vehicle performed reasonably well, using its exceptional speed to cover broad frontages, maintain contact with enemy forces, and conduct slashing attacks through Taurian and Magistracy formations. Star League observers noted the design's effectiveness as a picket and in high-speed offensive operations.

The vehicle's battlefield reputation was nonetheless tarnished by its reliability failures. SLDF analysts estimated that as many as one in ten deaths among Republican Hipparch crews resulted from mechanical malfunction rather than enemy fire, a damning indictment of the rushed production program. Star League technicians who observed the Hipparch's costly performance reportedly concluded the Republic's cavalry needed a more sound design, an assessment that contributed to the subsequent development of the J. Edgar hover tank.

The Hipparch also suffered from misapplication. Despite its light armor, Republican commanders increasingly assigned the vehicle as the anvil in heavy tank maneuvers, using the Hipparch's speed to encircle enemy formations while heavier vehicles delivered the killing blow. The tactic occasionally succeeded but inflicted heavy casualties on the cavalry when enemy armor turned to engage.

Of approximately 7,000 Hipparchs built, fewer than ninety survived the Reunification War. The production line was permanently destroyed in 2599 during the Wbika coup on Apollo, ending replacement production before most surviving vehicles had completed a decade of service.

text.deployment: The standard Hunter remains in production across multiple facilities and is found throughout the Inner Sphere and Periphery. Its broad availability through licensed manufacturers ensures that even the most cash-strapped militias can field effective long-range fire support. Examples of the original Hunter can be found in service with nearly every military that fields tracked combat vehicles.

The upgraded Hunter entered full production at Defiance Industries in late 3054, incorporating advances recovered from Star League-era technology caches. Twin Coventry Star Fire launchers with Artemis IV fire control doubled the design's missile accuracy. The first new Hunters arrived in Federated Commonwealth units in early 3055, with most deliveries going to Lyran formations. The slower engine and lighter ferro-fibrous armor made the upgraded Hunter more vulnerable than its predecessor, a trade-off that not all crews appreciated.

A common field modification dating to the early Succession Wars, this variant removes the rear-facing flamer in exchange for a third ton of LRM ammunition. Crews who preferred sustained bombardment over any pretense of close-range defense found the trade worthwhile, and the straightforward conversion required no specialized tools or facilities beyond a basic field workshop.

The most recent Hunter variant leverages Clan-specification equipment that became widely available during the Dark Age. A fuel cell engine provides exceptional speed for the weight class, while heavy ferro-fibrous armor offers improved protection. The Defiance-Doombud ClanTech LRM 20 launcher with Artemis IV fire control returns the design to its single-launcher roots with substantially improved accuracy. CASE-protected ammunition bins and a rear-mounted vehicle flamer round out the package.

First appearing in 3059, this variant of the upgraded Hunter replaces one Coventry Star Fire launcher with an extended-range large laser. Additional heat sinks offset the energy weapon's thermal output, and the conversion allows continued missile support alongside direct-fire capability at extended ranges. An extended-range large laser is the favored choice where the equipment is readily available.

Introduced in 3061, this variant swaps one missile launcher for a large pulse laser, pairing accurate energy fire with an expanded ammunition supply for the remaining launcher. The combination of reliable pulse laser accuracy and sustained missile fire makes this one of the more popular upgraded Hunter configurations where equipment is available.

This extensively reworked field variant downgrades the missile launcher to a ten-tube rack and fills the freed tonnage with two forward-mounted medium lasers and paired side-mounted machine guns. The result is a more versatile platform capable of meaningful self-defense at close range, though it sacrifices much of the Hunter's original long-range fire support capability in the process.

Similar in concept to the LRM-10 conversion, this field variant mounts a fifteen-tube launcher with two tons of ammunition and additional close-defense weapons. It retains more of the Hunter's original fire support capability than its smaller-racked sibling while still providing the crew with options against infantry and light vehicles that close to short range.

During the original RWR service period, the Ignis was restricted to elements of the state security apparatus and did not serve with regular military formations. When Stefan Amaris reintroduced the vehicle in 2751, he distributed it through the Amaris Dragoon regiments, ensuring each unit held at least one company of Ignis vehicles and most received in excess of a full battalion. The vehicle's persistent mechanical problems required unusual logistical arrangements. Units typically maintained vehicle pools numbering twice the available crews, ensuring that enough operational vehicles remained available at any given time regardless of how many were down for maintenance or repair.

The SRM configuration arose from recognition that the base Ignis was wholly incapable of engaging any opposition that refused to close to short range. Dropping one flamer from each side and reducing the flamer ammunition by three tons created space for a pair of SRM-2 launchers mounted in the turret, giving crews a meaningful option against light vehicles and BattleMechs. The twin ammunition bins proved highly adaptable, and crews routinely loaded non-standard warheads. Tear gas rounds were used to flush occupants from structures before the remaining flamers were applied. Fragmentation warheads provided antipersonnel coverage in more open areas. Inferno rounds quickly became the preferred loading among experienced Ignis crews, offering the incendiary effect of the vehicle's flamers at a range that kept the Ignis out of immediate return fire.

text.deployment: The standard Indra Infantry Transport serves primarily as an armored personnel carrier in Clan combined-arms Points and Stars, moving infantry between engagements and providing direct-fire support during dismounted operations. Its strong main armament allows it to contribute meaningfully in firefights rather than waiting at a standoff distance while passengers engage, though commanders must account for the vehicle's heat limitations in prolonged close combat. The standard variant serves across multiple Clan toumans with homeworld production spread across the Kerensky Cluster ensuring broad availability. The Quikscell Company facility on Pandora provides an additional production source beginning in the Civil War era, primarily serving Clan Jade Falcon and later Clan Wolf formations in occupation and garrison roles throughout the occupied Inner Sphere.

The (BA) variant was developed in 3069 to address the specialized demands of anti-insurgency and urban pacification operations, particularly in the aftermath of the Hell's Horses invasion of former Lyran worlds. This configuration retains the standard chassis but modifies the infantry bay and loadout to better accommodate battle armor operations and close-range anti-infantry engagements. Production is limited to the Quikscell Company facility on Pandora. The vehicle is issued primarily to Clan Wolf forces operating in occupation zones where anti-insurgency capability takes priority over conventional armored transport. The Indra's association with the Turtle Bay massacre creates a persistent public relations burden for units equipped with this variant, one that Wolf commanders have had limited success in addressing through rebranding or operational distinction.

The Ishtar (Gauss) emerged during the Jihad as Clan Hell's Horses sought to address the standard version's vulnerability against heavier Inner Sphere armor in renewed combat operations. Replacing both autocannons with a Gauss Rifle and a Class 20 Hyper-Assault Gauss Rifle at the cost of the anti-missile system, the variant concentrates its offensive capability into two high-velocity projectile weapons capable of penetrating heavy armor at range. Each weapon carries two tons of ammunition. Field refit kits supported deployment among Hell's Horses formations, supplemented by dedicated factory production at Csesztreg and Kirchbach. The Horses' open sales policy extended availability beyond their own touman, making this variant accessible to outside buyers through the same commercial channels as the standard model.

The Ishtar (Original) served as the first-generation heavy fire support platform across Clan homeworld garrison formations beginning in 2842. Its higher top speed suited offensive operations and rapid redeployment more than the later standard version, but commanders found its lighter armor and reduced weapons load a meaningful liability in sustained engagements. Clan Hell's Horses and Star Adder facilities documented factory lines for this variant, though neither recorded active production during the MUPL surveyed period. By the time the standard Ishtar entered service in 2976, the Original had been largely displaced on garrison rosters, surviving only in mothballed reserve units and training formations where its lighter loadout was considered adequate for low-threat environments.

The standard J-27 is found everywhere in the Inner Sphere and beyond. All Great Houses have manufacturers producing the design, as do the larger Periphery nations. Acme's licensing fees were so low that no manufacturer felt the need to redesign the transport beyond cosmetic changes to nameplates and logos. Among smaller Periphery realms and lawless frontier regions, the J-27 is considered a valuable commodity.

The (Armor) variant adds heavier protection at the expense of some cargo capacity. Introduced during the Succession Wars as a common field modification, it reflects the harsh reality that J-27 crews operating near active combat zones needed more than a half-ton of plating between themselves and enemy fire. The modification is straightforward enough to be performed by any competent vehicle technician.

The (Fusion) variant replaces the standard internal combustion engine with a scavenged fusion powerplant. These tend to be original Star League era vehicles that have survived the ages. The fusion engine frees the vehicle from dependence on fossil fuel supply lines, a significant logistical advantage that makes surviving examples highly prized.

text.deployment: The standard J. Edgar serves primarily as a fast cavalry and raiding platform. Taurian Defense Force formations used it extensively during the New Vandenburg Revolt, where it proved effective as a core element of light armor formations. Federated Suns commanders concentrate the vehicle in companies attached to elite fast units such as the Avalon Hussars and Deneb Light Cavalry rather than distributing it among general armor formations. The Com Guards also field a limited number drawn from Star League-era stockpiles on Terra.

Developed by Scarborough Manufacturers in 3088, this fuel cell-powered variant was designed to enable production at small automotive repair facilities, reducing dependence on heavy industrial infrastructure in the post-Jihad era. The turret mounts a medium chemical laser and SRM 4, supplemented by two machine guns for anti-infantry coverage. Five and a half tons of heavy ferro-fibrous armor provide solid protection. It is found primarily in Draconis Combine and former Republic of the Sphere formations that adopted the design following Scarborough's production restart in the Dark Age.

This 2793 field modification replaces the SRM 2 racks with a pair of vehicle flamers. It sees use primarily in anti-infantry and defoliant operations where clearing vegetation or fortified positions takes priority over anti-armor work. Found most commonly in secondary garrison forces and militia units that lack regular access to missile resupply, the Flamer variant sacrifices the design's modest anti-armor capability for a role-specialized weapons fit.

production.manufacturer: Alphard Trading Corporation|Alphard Trading Corporation|Field Refit

text.deployment: The ICE conversion emerged from battlefield necessity in 2854, as field technicians substituted available internal combustion engines for damaged fusion powerplants. The resulting vehicle operates at a reduced flank speed of 129 kilometers per hour and carries one ton less armor than the standard. It is found widely in Periphery garrison forces, planetary militias, and any formation that cannot sustain fusion power systems. The Marian Hegemony's Alphard Trading Company eventually standardized this configuration as a factory production variant.

Produced by Scarborough Manufacturers on Al Na'ir beginning in 3053, this Draconis Combine refit replaces the SRM 2 launchers with two additional medium lasers and a small laser while integrating a C3 slave unit. Six tons of ferro-fibrous armor improve survivability over the standard model. Assigned to Combine C3 networks, the vehicle serves as a fast networked scout that shares targeting data across lance-level formations equipped with C3 master units, multiplying the effectiveness of cooperative fire.

The Marian Hegemony's Alphard Trading Company introduced this updated ICE variant in 3070, replacing the laser and missile armament with a Light Autocannon/5 and four Rocket Launcher 10s. Four and a half tons of heavy ferro-fibrous armor provide improved protection over the earlier ICE model. Designed for Periphery operations where sophisticated power systems are difficult to sustain, the LAC variant serves Marian forces as a light direct fire and anti-infantry platform capable of independent operation far from major supply centers.

Produced by StarCorps Industries on Crofton beginning in 3085, this variant upgrades the primary weapon to a Light PPC connected to a targeting computer, while the missile launchers are downgraded to improved one-shot versions to save tonnage. Five and a half tons of heavy ferro-fibrous armor improve survivability over the standard model. Avalon Hussars units fielded examples against Draconis Combine forces on Robinson in February 3150, where the Light PPC's extended range and improved accuracy proved effective against fast-moving Combine armor.

Dating to 2794, this variant replaces each SRM 2 rack with a pair of machine guns, optimizing the vehicle for anti-infantry and anti-battle armor work. The battery of four machine guns delivers punishing fire against soft targets and light infantry vehicles. Deployed in infantry support and urban security roles where armor threats are minimal, the MG variant sees service across a wide range of factions and eras as a straightforward and inexpensive weapons substitution.

Produced by StarCorps Industries on Crofton beginning in 3053, this variant replaces the SRM 2 racks with a TAG designator and a Beagle Active Probe while retaining a pair of medium lasers for self-defense. It serves as a forward spotter for artillery and indirect fire assets, penetrating enemy lines to designate targets for guided munitions. The Avalon Hussars and other elite AFFS formations fielded this variant extensively during the Clan Invasion period and subsequent conflicts, exploiting its speed to operate ahead of slower fire-support platforms.

text.deployment: The X-Pulse returns to fusion-powered performance while modernizing the armament with a Diverse Optics Type 25PX Medium X-Pulse Laser. The ProtecTech 19 heavy ferro-fibrous armor provides greater protection per ton than the original StarSlab arrangement. Produced across seven facilities spanning the Marian Hegemony, Taurian Concordat, Fronc Reaches, Free Worlds League, Federated Suns, and Draconis Combine, the X-Pulse serves as a first-line reconnaissance asset across a wide range of political boundaries, reflecting the design's enduring utility as a fast strike platform.

text.overview: The Jagdpanzer II, marketed under the FrontierTech brand name, is an experimental enhancement to the Hetzer Wheeled Assault Gun chassis addressing the two most criticised limitations of the original design: inadequate closing speed and short battlefield endurance. Introduced during the Jihad in 3074, the vehicle was developed by an undisclosed producer whose identity, production site, and technical staff remained classified at the time of its field testing summation. The result is a substantially more capable platform that retains the Hetzer's basic wheeled configuration while correcting its most dangerous tactical shortcomings.
text.capabilities:
The Jagdpanzer II replaces the Hetzer's conventional internal combustion engine with a 180-rated extralight fusion powerplant, raising flank speed to 86.4 km/h, twenty kilometres per hour faster than the original. The fusion engine also eliminates the endurance constraints imposed by the ICE, allowing the vehicle to sustain operations without fuel resupply. The primary weapon is a Defiance Thunder Ultra Autocannon/20, which offers thirty metres more effective range than the Crusher and doubles the firing rate. With four tons of ammunition, the Jagdpanzer II can sustain the weapon through extended engagements where the original design would have depleted its stores quickly.

The most significant defensive upgrade is six tons of vehicular stealth armor, derived from Capellan BattleMech stealth technology adapted to ground vehicle use. Combined with a Guardian ECM suite, the stealth system makes targeting the Jagdpanzer II substantially more difficult than normal, compensating for the chassis's continued lack of a turret. Two Sperry-Browning machine guns mounted in sponson turrets on either flank provide close-in protection against infantry. The stealth armor and ECM do impose heat management demands the original Hetzer never faced, and the experimental status of the vehicular stealth system meant availability was limited. The vehicle is expensive to produce and maintain relative to the baseline Hetzer, undermining the original design's core appeal of low cost and simplicity.
text.deployment: The Jagdpanzer II is suited to aggressive ambush and raiding roles that the standard Hetzer cannot reliably perform. Its speed allows it to close with targets, deliver concentrated Ultra Autocannon fire, and withdraw before return fire can be effectively directed. The stealth armor and Guardian ECM make it difficult to target at range, enabling approaches through terrain that would be suicidal for a standard Hetzer. It is rarely found in the planetary militia and garrison roles typical of its progenitor, instead appearing in specialist raiding formations or as a high-value asset in combined-arms lances. Universal availability means it can appear across faction lines, though sightings remain uncommon given its cost and experimental origins.
text.battleHistory:
The Jagdpanzer II emerged from a recognised tactical problem. Hetzer crews and their commanders had understood from the beginning that the vehicle's thin armor and low speed made it a liability in open terrain. Decades of field doctrine had managed the problem through careful positioning and massed deployment, but these workarounds accepted significant constraints on how and where the chassis could be employed. An unknown producer, working through the FrontierTech commercial testing framework during the Jihad, pursued a more direct solution by rebuilding the vehicle around an extralight fusion engine and experimental stealth armor.

The field testing summation that documented the Jagdpanzer II was deliberately obscure about its origins. The producer, production site, supervising technician, and project start date were all withheld by request. Transit to the testing location was arranged aboard Gazelle-class DropShips under non-disclosure agreements, and participants were required to sign non-competitive contracts and trade-secret guarantees before embarking. This level of operational security was unusual even for experimental programs during the Jihad, and suggested either a politically sensitive production arrangement or a producer operating in contested territory. The vehicle's use of vehicular stealth armor, still experimental at the time of the field test, pointed toward connections with the Capellan Confederation's stealth technology programs, though no direct link was confirmed.

The design entered small-scale Universal availability after the Jihad, spreading through salvage and knowledge transfer as the stealth armor technology became less restricted. Its high cost relative to the standard Hetzer limited adoption to units that specifically valued the stealth and speed improvements over the baseline's simplicity. It remained a rare and specialised platform rather than the mass-produced garrison vehicle its progenitor had become.

text.deployment: The base JES I saw continuous production from Panpour beginning in 3075. Despite its poor reputation among mainstream military analysts, the vehicle proved popular with Periphery states and mercenary commands operating on tight budgets. The Taurian Concordat and Calderon Protectorate were early volume buyers, and Republic of the Sphere militia units adopted the carrier after the HPG Blackout in 3132, when supply chains collapsed and cheap, available hardware became essential.

The 3082 Upgrade addressed the JES I's most notorious shortcoming by replacing the tiny JES 15 engine with a 165-rated powerplant produced at JES's expanded Cartago engine facility. The upgraded vehicle was built on a tracked chassis rather than the original hovercraft platform, and the larger engine increased maximum speed substantially. Despite a nearly sixty percent increase in unit cost, the upgraded version saw strong sales and became a common support element in JES II platoons.

production.communications: Communicator with Guardian ECM and C3 Slave

text.deployment: The base JES II entered service in 3079 at Panpour and Alula Australis simultaneously. Ghost Bear Dominion forces and the Federated Suns were the primary operators, with the Suns integrating the carriers into defensive formations and the Dominion deploying them to reinforce garrison forces. Republic of the Sphere militia units also adopted the design in significant numbers, and the Zebebelgenubi facility served Republic demand directly.

The Ammo variant was developed in 3080 for the Ghost Bear Dominion. Dominion units did not use Spheroid C3 networking systems, so the C3 slave was removed and replaced with an additional ton of LRM ammunition. This simple modification increased the vehicle's sustained fire capability, better suiting the Dominion's preferred doctrine of massed indirect fire from prepared positions. Production was centered at Panpour.

The Support variant, introduced in 3088, revisited JES's original LRM carrier concept by significantly increasing the missile payload at the expense of all electronic warfare systems and most armor protection. Stripped of its Guardian ECM and C3 slave, the Support variant traded survivability for raw firepower, appealing to commanders who needed maximum missile volume from static defensive positions where electronic countermeasures were less critical. All three JES facilities produced this variant.

The standard JES III entered service in 3133 from Zebebelgenubi, with Alula Australis and Panpour adding production shortly afterward. Republic militia forces were the initial primary operators, but the vehicle spread rapidly to Federated Suns, Dominion, and Clan Jade Falcon forces as the Dark Age intensified. The design's ease of maintenance and reliable performance made it a favorite among garrison commanders across the Inner Sphere.

The C3 variant, introduced in 3140, reduces LRM ammunition by one ton to make room for a C3 slave networking unit. This modification enables the JES III to share targeting data with C3-equipped lancemates, significantly improving fire accuracy when paired with forward spotters. The variant saw particular adoption among Federated Suns and Republic successor forces that maintained C3 network infrastructure.

text.capabilities:
The JES III mounts four turret-mounted FarFire LRM-15 launchers as its primary armament, giving it a combined barrage of sixty missiles per salvo. The turret mount is a significant tactical advantage over the fixed-forward launchers of earlier JES designs, allowing the crew to engage targets across a full arc without repositioning the vehicle. Two GM MiniGun machine guns provide point defense against infantry, though the JES III lacks any meaningful secondary weapons beyond these. A six-ton ammunition bay provides reasonable endurance for sustained bombardment missions.

A GM 160 XL fusion engine gives the wheeled carrier a top speed of 54 km/h, modest but adequate for a fire support platform that typically operates from the second echelon. Starshield III armor provides protection appropriate to the vehicle's support role, though crews are expected to avoid direct engagement with frontline combatants. The Communicator communications system and FireScan with IndirecTrack targeting system are the same proven electronics suite used across the entire JES carrier line, simplifying logistics and crew training. Whatever lessons Joint Equipment Systems learned building their earlier carriers paid dividends with the JES III, which earned design quirks for both ease of maintenance and improved long-range targeting accuracy.
text.deployment: The MML variant replaces the four LRM-15 launchers with four MML-9 multi-missile launchers and adds a pair of extended-range medium lasers. The multi-missile launchers sacrifice raw long-range volume for tactical flexibility, allowing crews to switch between LRM and SRM ammunition loads to match engagement conditions. A reduced four-ton missile bay reflects the lighter per-launcher ammunition requirements. Introduced in 3133 alongside the base model, this variant was produced at all three JES facilities.

The Speed variant, introduced in 3135, removes the machine guns and their ammunition to accommodate a larger engine, boosting the JES III's top speed to 64 km/h. While modest by combat vehicle standards, the improved mobility allows the carrier to reposition more quickly between fire missions and keep pace with faster formation elements. The loss of anti-infantry capability was considered an acceptable trade by most operators. All three JES facilities produced this variant.

The Thunderbolt variant swaps the four FarFire LRM-15 launchers for four Thunderbolt 10 missile launchers. The Thunderbolt missiles sacrifice volume of fire for per-missile accuracy and hitting power, delivering focused strikes against hardened targets rather than area saturation. Introduced in 3133, this variant was produced at all three JES facilities and found favor with commanders who needed precision fire support rather than area suppression.

The standard JI2A1 serves primarily as a battle armor transport in Federated Suns combined-arms formations, with particular concentration in commands that favor aggressive hover operations. The vehicle performs best when paired with fire support assets capable of engaging targets at extended range, allowing the APC to sprint into assault positions under covering fire. Crews typically load their SRM magazines with specialty ammunition selected to match anticipated opposition before each operation. The JI2A1 functions well in urban and broken terrain, where its compact profile and maneuverability partially offset the loss of open-ground speed advantage. It is unsuited to independent operations against prepared defensive lines or sustained engagements at standoff distances.

The (MML) variant replaces the standard SRM turret with a pair of multi-missile launchers, extending the vehicle's effective engagement range while retaining close-range capability. This expanded envelope makes the MML variant a more independent platform, capable of contributing to fire missions after deploying its battle armor element rather than relying on attached support units for long-range coverage. Johnston Industries offers the configuration both as a production option and as an after-market retrofit package, making it practical for commands seeking to upgrade existing JI2A1 fleets without full replacement. The MML variant is particularly valued in lighter formations where the APC may be the heaviest direct-fire asset available for portions of an engagement.

text.overview: The Joust Medium Tank is Clan Nova Cat's second purpose-built combat vehicle designed for Inner Sphere service, produced at the Barcella Beta facility on Irece beginning in 3077. Intended to complement the heavier assault Starmates of the Nova Cat touman, the Joust delivers protection and firepower that far exceed expectations for its forty-ton frame. The design is a deliberate effort by Clan Nova Cat's scientific and merchant castes to expand their vehicle offerings for both the Nova Cat military and prospective Inner Sphere buyers. Though development was hampered by the Jihad, the finished product proved worth the delay. Since entering service, the Joust has earned a reputation as a reliable fire support and escort vehicle capable of accompanying even the heaviest assault formations.
text.capabilities:
Despite its forty-ton frame, the Joust is built more like a heavy tank than a medium combatant. Almost ten tons of Advanced Compound Beta ferro-fibrous armor encases the hull, providing protection that rivals many vehicles an entire weight class above. This survivability forms the foundation of the Joust's tactical identity, allowing it to absorb punishment while its weapons do their work.

The primary armament is a turret-mounted Series 7NC ER Large Laser, a weapon with sufficient range and hitting power to threaten even the heaviest assault BattleMechs. The laser requires no ammunition, freeing mass for additional protection. A Type 9 Series 1 ATM 9 launcher complements the laser with variable-effect missiles, supported by three separate ammunition magazines that allow gunners to select standard, extended-range, or high-explosive rounds as the situation demands. Four Series 2c light machine guns are distributed across the hull to discourage infantry threats. The weapon arrangement is effective, though the Joust lacks any meaningful point-defense capability and remains vulnerable when its infantry screen is absent.

The vehicle's principal limitation is speed. Its 200 XL fusion engine delivers a road speed below that of many vehicles at comparable mass, a deliberate trade for the armor load. Placed alongside heavier assault elements such as the Mars or Ishtar Starmates, this limitation largely disappears, as the Joust is fast enough to keep pace with those machines and serve as heavy cavalry. Against swifter opponents, the Joust depends on its thick armor and the gunner's long-range precision rather than maneuver, and commanders must plan accordingly.
text.deployment: The BE700 entered full production at Barcella Beta on Irece in 3077 and was quickly distributed across the Nova Cat touman, with Stars shipped to every major second-line Cluster and front-line formation. Units reached Draconis Combine formations through operational transfers, reflecting the Nova Cats' integrated relationship with DC forces after the Civil War. The Republic Armed Forces pursued procurement negotiations with the Nova Cat merchant caste following the Joust's performance along the Capellan border, with the Hastati Sentinels and Triarii Protectors identified as high-priority recipients.
text.battleHistory:
The origins of the Joust trace to the battlefield performance of the SM1 tank destroyer, whose success in Nova Cat service and commercial markets demonstrated that the Nova Cat merchant caste could compete in the Inner Sphere vehicle industry. Clan Nova Cat's scientists and industry leaders moved to develop a follow-on design for a different tactical niche, providing medium-weight fire support and escort that the SM1's heavier frame could not economically fill.

Development began with ambitious timelines that the Jihad disrupted. The conflict that consumed the Inner Sphere from 3068 onward strained manufacturing networks and Nova Cat operational priorities alike. Barcella Beta on Irece survived as an operational facility, but wartime demands and resource competition delayed the Joust's introduction by several years. The first completed vehicle did not roll off the assembly line until 3077, nearly a decade after initial design work had begun.

Questions about quality surfaced relatively soon after the Joust entered service. Reports from Triarii Protectors in Republic service described the ER Large Laser system misfiring without trigger input. Nova Cat engineers initially attributed the complaints to inexperience among the Triarii's crews, a characterization that appeared plausible given the Triarii's reputation as the least combat-experienced formation in the Republic Armed Forces. The explanation grew harder to sustain when similar reports emerged from Draconis Combine formations within two months, suggesting a genuine production defect rather than crew error. The episode marked the first quality dispute involving an Irece manufacturer since the Nova Cats established control of the planet, and it prompted quiet internal reviews at Barcella Beta.

text.overview: The Kalki Cruise Missile Launcher is a superheavy tracked vehicle designed by Kallon Industries to deploy cruise missile artillery from a mobile ground platform. Named for the Hindu deity, the 150-ton Kalki represents one of the very few successful attempts to field these massive weapons outside of DropShip or fixed installations. Cruise missiles are enormous unguided artillery weapons derived from Arrow IV technology, capable of devastating area bombardment at extreme range. The sheer destructive power and psychological impact of these weapons prompted intense competition among Federated Suns defense contractors when the AFFS revived research into the technology in the 3060s. Kallon Industries was the first company to field a working prototype, and the production model entered service in 3079 after a complete redesign of the original experimental concept.
text.capabilities:
The production Kalki mounts a single Excelsior I Cruise Missile/50 launcher as its primary weapon, capable of delivering devastating area bombardment at extreme range. Each missile weighs roughly as much as a light BattleMech, and the vehicle carries only a single reload. This severe ammunition limitation means the Kalki must be externally resupplied after every second shot, requiring dedicated logistics support that complicates field deployment. A Locom 300 fuel cell powerplant keeps costs manageable but limits the vehicle to a crawling top speed, effectively excluding it from mobile formations.

Seven tons of StarSlab/7 armor provides reasonable protection, though the vehicle's massive 150-ton hull means coverage is spread thin across all facings. Two Federated-Barrett Magshot Gauss Rifles offer minimal self-defense against infantry or light vehicles. The JoLex Systems communications suite and StratSight v.9 targeting system provide the precision needed for cruise missile delivery. The Kalki's principal strengths lie in the sheer destructive power and morale impact of its payload, while its slow speed, limited ammunition, and thin relative armor represent significant tactical vulnerabilities that require careful mission planning and dedicated escort forces.
text.deployment: The production Kalki operates exclusively within the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, manufactured at the Kallon Industries facility on Kirklin. The AFFS High Command has restricted the vehicle to premier combat formations since accepting delivery in 3079, denying repeated requests from mercenary commands. Commanders who receive the Kalki often struggle with its operational limitations, frequently waiting for the perfect moment to deploy its devastating payload rather than acting on available opportunities.
text.battleHistory:
Cruise missile technology had been abandoned for centuries before the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns revived research in 3065. These weapons deliver devastating area destruction and profound psychological impact on enemy formations, but their sheer size, with individual missiles weighing as much as a Commando BattleMech, made integration into conventional ground vehicles an enormous engineering challenge.

Kallon Industries began the original Kalki project in 3068 using a modified SturmFeur chassis, but the experimental prototype suffered from critical engineering failures and was shelved in the early 3070s. By the late 3070s, Kallon restarted the program with a completely redesigned 150-ton vehicle that shared components with the SturmFeur but featured a purpose-built chassis and a fuel cell powerplant. The AFFS accepted delivery in 3079 and has since maintained exclusive control over the weapon system. Mercenary commands, particularly the Illician Lancers and Vegan Rangers, have repeatedly requested access, but the AFFS High Command has tightly restricted deployment to its premier formations.

text.deployment: The A Configuration converts the Kamisori into a dedicated sniper platform. The modular turret mounts a Light PPC fitted with a PPC Capacitor, pairing variable-output firepower with a Targeting Computer that compensates for the vehicle's modest baseline targeting suite. The result is a vehicle capable of delivering precise fire at ranges that outstrip most light vehicle opposition, while remaining difficult to pin down. The A is often deployed on the flanks of militia defensive lines, harassing advancing forces before repositioning. The reliance on a single weapon remains a constraint, but the configuration's accuracy and range make it a disproportionate threat for its size class.

The B Configuration prioritizes mobility above all else, equipping the Kamisori with a Supercharger that briefly pushes the engine beyond its standard performance envelope. The primary weapon is a Medium Variable Speed Pulse Laser, a flexible direct-fire system that adjusts its damage spread based on engagement range. The combination suits rapid strike missions, where the vehicle dashes forward, delivers concentrated fire, and withdraws before heavier units can respond effectively. Commanders have learned to hold B-configured Kamisoris in reserve until a clear opportunity presents itself, rather than committing them to sustained engagements their limited armament cannot support.

The C Configuration sacrifices almost all offensive capability to transform the Kamisori into a battlefield electronics node. An Active Probe extends the vehicle's sensor reach well beyond normal parameters, while a C3 Slave Unit allows the tank to share targeting data with coordinating lance members. The ECM Suite provides passive protection against enemy guidance and targeting systems. The sole weapon is a turret-mounted ER Medium Laser adequate for self-defense, not engagement. C-configured Kamisoris are typically screened by more heavily armed lancemates and positioned with command elements. Their true value emerges in C3-networked formations, where the shared targeting data multiplies the accuracy of the entire lance.

The Prime Configuration loads the Kamisori's five-ton bay with a single Large Laser, giving planetary militia units a reliable direct-fire weapon that requires no ammunition supply chain. The straightforward loadout suits patrol and screening duties, where a single powerful shot at moderate range deters light raider vehicles and infantry without demanding the tactical sophistication of more specialized configurations. Militia formations often employ Prime Kamisoris as the backbone of a mixed lance, pairing them with more specialized configurations to cover sensor or anti-infantry gaps.

The R Configuration integrates Clan-sourced weaponry, mounting a Plasma Cannon with two tons of ammunition in place of standard Inner Sphere systems. The Plasma Cannon excels at anti-infantry, anti-Battle Armor, and anti-vehicle work, combining heat-inducing effects against BattleMechs with destructive fragmentation damage against softer targets. The configuration was designed with the Combine's combined-arms doctrine in mind: deployed alongside standard infantry or battle armor squads, R-configured Kamisoris handle the armored threats conventional infantry cannot engage directly. Availability of Clan-sourced ammunition has posed logistical challenges in forward militia units, though DCMS supply chains have adapted to support the configuration in most active theater deployments.

The Kanga served the SLDF Vehicle Corps as a premier reconnaissance and fire support asset from its introduction through the Star League era, its jump capability allowing it to support BattleMech operations in terrain where conventional vehicles could not follow. Survivors passed to ComStar's reserves following the Succession Wars. The Com Guards deployed the remaining operational examples during the FedCom Civil War, and a small number of original models also survived in Clan Homeworlds caches, retained by Clan Hell's Horses as engineering reference material and occasional operational assets.

The autocannon variant emerged during the early Succession Wars as maintaining the original AL2200 jump AI system became increasingly impractical across the Inner Sphere and Pentagon Worlds. Technicians stripped the jump jets and SRM launchers from damaged or partially functional Kangas, replacing the autocannon with a heavier weapon and redistributing the freed mass to thicken the side armor. The resulting vehicle traded the Kanga's signature tactical capability for a more conventional and maintainable hovertank profile, sacrificing jump mobility in exchange for operational reliability during a period of severe technological decline.

text.overview: The Karnov UR Gunship is a common field conversion of the ubiquitous Karnov UR Transport, sacrificing the aircraft's cargo bay to mount machine gun emplacements. The modification gained popularity during the War of 3039, when demand for armed aerial support outpaced the availability of purpose-built combat VTOLs. Field technicians across the Inner Sphere independently developed similar configurations, mounting pairs of machine guns in each former cargo bay with supporting ammunition stores. The Gunship conversion trades the Karnov's utility as a transport for a modest but useful anti-infantry and anti-soft-target capability, filling a gap in units that lack dedicated attack helicopter assets. The modification requires no exotic parts or specialized tooling, making it accessible to militia forces, mercenary commands, and garrison units operating far from major supply depots.
text.capabilities:
The Gunship conversion retains the base Karnov's DAV 190 ICE engine, tilt-rotor assembly, and StarSlab armor, inheriting all the structural characteristics and limitations of the transport variant. The primary modification replaces the six-ton cargo hold with four machine gun installations, two in each former bay position, supported by two tons of ammunition. The machine guns provide effective suppressive fire against infantry, unarmored vehicles, and exposed personnel, though they lack the punch to threaten even lightly armored combat vehicles.

Without the weight of cargo, the Gunship maintains the Karnov's full speed performance, making it an effective strafing platform against soft targets. The Johnston Q-Rotor communications system carries over unchanged, though many Gunship crews supplement it with additional radio equipment scavenged from ground vehicles. The Gunship retains the Karnov's primary vulnerability: its oversized rotors remain exposed to ground fire, and a single well-placed hit can bring the aircraft down regardless of its armament. Crews compensate with aggressive low-altitude tactics and the aircraft's high speed, relying on brief, violent strafing runs rather than sustained loiter over hostile positions.
text.deployment: The standard Gunship conversion, mounting four machine guns with two tons of ammunition in the former cargo bays. As a field refit requiring no specialized parts, the Gunship can be produced by any competent maintenance team with access to a Karnov transport and basic machine gun mounts. The variant serves primarily with militia forces, garrison commands, and mercenary units across the Inner Sphere, providing low-cost aerial fire support for ground operations.
text.battleHistory:
The Karnov UR Gunship emerged organically during the War of 3039, when Inner Sphere forces found themselves short of dedicated combat VTOLs to support ground operations. Garrison commanders and mercenary technicians independently arrived at the same solution: strip the cargo bay from a surplus or damaged Karnov and install whatever weapons were available. A common upgrade that made the rounds during this period mounted two Sperry-Browning machine guns in each arc, and the four-gun configuration became the standardized Gunship pattern.

The conversion proved popular enough that it spread rapidly through informal channels, with field maintenance manuals and modification guides circulating among technical personnel across multiple factions. Unlike many field conversions that fade from use once purpose-built alternatives become available, the Karnov Gunship persisted because of its simplicity and the Karnov transport's sheer ubiquity. Any unit with a spare Karnov and a machine shop could produce a Gunship in days, without specialized parts or factory support.

The Gunship saw extensive use during the Clan Invasion, the FedCom Civil War, and the Jihad, wherever forward units needed aerial fire support and lacked the logistics chain to acquire dedicated attack helicopters. Militia units defending against bandit raids proved particularly fond of the conversion, as it provided an air support capability far beyond what most garrison forces could otherwise field. The Gunship remains in service across the Inner Sphere, proof of the base Karnov's adaptability and the enduring reality that military forces will always need more combat aircraft than their supply chains can provide.

text.deployment: The standard production Karnov, unchanged from its original ComStar-supplied configuration. As the most widely distributed variant, the base model serves in logistics and transport roles across every Successor State and many mercenary commands. Its combination of speed, cargo capacity, and low maintenance requirements makes it the default choice for rear-area supply missions and civilian cargo operations alike. Because its primary role is as a transport vehicle, armored for fast battlefield insertions and fitted with independent cargo handling features, the Karnov is not designed for frontline combat duties. Despite this, some mercenary and "kamikaze" combat logistic groups have managed to make a name for themselves using the Karnov in aggressive forward delivery roles.

The first factory variant produced at NETC's New Earth facility, introduced in 3055. The upgrade addresses the two most common complaints from military operators: the lack of defensive armament and the dangerously sensitive tilt-rotor system. ScatterGun light machine guns mounted on each side of the fuselage provide minimal defensive fire, while a switch to ferro-fibrous armor slightly increases protection levels. The most significant improvement is a rotor auto-adjustment sensor mounted on the fuselage bottom that detects ground proximity and automatically corrects rotor pitch, preventing the landing accidents that have destroyed countless Karnovs. A lighter DAV 160 gas turbine engine replaces the original DAV 190, reducing top speed somewhat but the added safety features and defensive armament more than compensate for the trade. The seven-ton cargo bay is slightly larger than the original model.

A common field modification that replaces the Karnov's cargo bay with an autocannon/20 installation and two tons of ammunition. A fusion engine replaces the standard ICE power plant to meet the energy demands of the heavier weapons system. The added weight of armament reduces cruising speed to roughly 86 kilometers per hour, but the devastating close-range firepower transforms the transport into a credible fire-support platform. Field technicians across the Inner Sphere have produced countless variations on this basic armed conversion configuration.

Similar to the AC conversion, this field modification mounts a Thumper artillery piece with twenty rounds of ammunition in place of the autocannon. The fusion engine swap provides necessary power, while the Thumper's indirect fire capability allows the Karnov to deliver artillery support from positions concealed behind terrain features. The combination of VTOL mobility and artillery has proven particularly effective in rapid repositioning during mobile engagements, allowing militia and mercenary forces to provide fire support that would otherwise require dedicated artillery vehicles.

The Republic of the Sphere's advanced stealth transport variant, produced at the Terran NETC facility. Vehicular stealth armor with a Guardian ECM suite renders the aircraft extremely difficult to detect during insertion and extraction operations. The ten-ton cargo bay accommodates even Clan assault-class battle armor, making it ideal for moving Spheroid battle armor and special forces alike. Maintaining cruise speeds matching the original Karnov, the BA Stealth variant emphasizes survivability at the cost of weaponry. The Republic prioritized acquiring the Karnov's production plans and facilities specifically to develop this variant, viewing stealthy battle armor delivery as a critical capability for its combined-arms doctrine. The market potential for aftersales packages has proven considerable.

NETC's purpose-built battle armor transport variant, mounting a fusion engine, Guardian ECM suite, and twin ER medium lasers. The eight-ton cargo bay accommodates two full squads of battle armor for rapid tactical deployment. The Guardian ECM provides electronic warfare protection during insertion runs, while the lasers suppress enemy positions as battle armor disembarks. Introduced in 3063, the BA variant quickly became popular with not only special operations units but also conventional infantry commands seeking high-speed transport for heavier assault squads. An extra half-ton of ferro-fibrous armor over the base model improves survivability during the critical moments of troop delivery.

A quick-strike variant popular among Periphery states and pirate bands, sacrificing all cargo capacity to mount an enormous battery of rocket launchers. Four rocket launcher 20s and six rocket launcher 10s fire forward in a single devastating salvo. With only one and a half tons of standard armor, the Periphery variant relies entirely on speed and the element of surprise, typically making a single attack run against supply convoys before retreating. The variant saw widespread adoption along Periphery border regions where traditional military procurement was impractical, and pirate groups favor the configuration for raids against escorts of supply convoys.

text.deployment: The standard Kestrel is deployed almost exclusively by specialized commands with the training and operational security needed to use it effectively. Its covert transport role requires small, disciplined insertion teams and experienced pilots capable of sustained nap-of-earth flight. Units lacking these prerequisites often find the vehicle's minimal armament and thin armor more liability than asset.

The Clan-tech refit emerged from the Dragoons' post-invasion access to advanced components, improving performance while preserving the original mission profile. Production was limited to the Blackwell facility on Outreach, and examples remained effectively exclusive to Wolf's Dragoons and their successor formations through the Civil War period. The variant was not observed in other hands.

The MedEvac variant replaces all weapons and most of the troop compartment with paramedic equipment capable of handling a squad of critical-need patients. A single recording confirmed factory production rather than field modification, taken during a Rabid Fox hostage extraction on an unidentified world believed to be in Capellan space. The variant was manufactured at both the Blackwell plant on Outreach and the General Motors/Blackwell facility on New Valencia. Its unarmed status demands capable escort whenever it operates in contested airspace.
